# DFS system: current architecture, defect audit, and greenfield specification

**Execution date:** September 8, 2026, verified from the Windows runtime (America/Chicago).  
**Repository:** `C:\Users\benja\Documents\Claude\mlb-dfs`  
**Reviewed commit:** `15f87a240bf7ecfbe7bdbc6bb7d6d332de2acf06`, branch `main`, including the existing working-tree changes.  
**Mandate:** read-only analysis. This dated document is the sole workspace deliverable; proposed code below has not been installed.

The current system is a substantial MLB Classic/Showdown construction, allocation, provenance, and export system. Its objective functions are deterministic projection and contest-shape proxies. It is **not a calibrated expected-dollar-return engine**, and neither an optimal MILP result nor a passing CSV proves that it is. The largest remaining risks are inconsistent evidence gates, incomplete immutable-run contracts, disagreement between late-swap validators, incomplete cache identity, and orchestration that still confuses some computational failures with strategic infeasibility.

The target should preserve the useful deterministic components while replacing their trust boundaries and orchestration. “Maximum EV, sub-second, zero touch” needs three explicit qualifications: EV must be estimated and validated against actual contest settlement; sub-second response is a measurable warm-state service objective, not a guarantee for arbitrary cold optimization; and automated submission requires a platform-authorized interface. DraftKings' published Daily Fantasy Terms prohibit automated website interaction, including lineup creation/editing, and automated collection of website information. No authorized submission API was established in this audit. Local processing can be autonomous now; an unattended DraftKings website bot is not the proposed deployment. [DraftKings Daily Fantasy Terms, Conditions of Participation](https://www.draftkings.com/help/terms).

Static coverage consists of a whole-tree inventory, AST/function and exception/call-site indexing, schema inspection, and detailed tracing of production paths and relevant regression tests. It does **not** establish that every one of 104,090 source lines is defect-free or that every archived artifact has been semantically certified. Vendored SciPy source is inventoried as a dependency, not audited as original application code. Ignored patch/mutation scripts are indexed as historical tools, not executed. Runtime probes using pandas used explicit compatible fixture dtypes; passing on the supplemental runtime is not a substitute for the pinned runtime.

The five tracked modifications present at intake were the batting and pitching expected-stat tables, FanGraphs platoon JSON, reference manifest, and awaiting-standings document. Numerous pre-existing untracked artifacts and older specifications were also present. They are preserved. The previous September 3 audit was used to locate historical questions; every finding asserted here is supported by current code or current probes. Older findings that were repaired are explicitly separated below.

### 1.4 Baseline data flow

```text
User/platform salary + reserved-entry CSVs     External MLB/odds/weather/reference sources
                    |                                          |
        stage_slate / build_slate               fetch_slate_bundle / paste adapters
                    |                                          |
                    +---- salary/feed reconciliation ----------+
                                      |
                         format + draftgroup + clock
                    /                                     \
              MLB Classic                              MLB Showdown
          build_slate_pool                         melt CPT/UTIL salary pairs
          projection factors                       APPG Base + thesis multipliers
          ownership/leverage                       captain/player exposure holds
          bank_cache + single MILPs                sequential Showdown MILPs
                    |                                     |
        joint entry allocation MILP                      bank[j] -> entry[j]
                    |                                     |
        execute_portfolio / run state             Showdown template writer
                    \                                     /
                        final CSV + brief + diagnostics
                                      |
                          run / delivery manifests
                                      |
                 preflight_upload + verify_export + QA
                                      |
                          manual platform submission
                                      |
             standings -> field_miner -> ownership grading -> ledger

Late swap: parent export + current feed -> lock map -> mutable-entry requirements
           -> regenerate/allocate against fixed rows -> final-file/parent checks
           -> promotion/delivery -> same platform boundary
```

This is not one transactional DAG. Different entry points resolve feeds, clocks, parent files, status flags, model labels and manifests separately. That duplication is the origin of several apparently unrelated defects below.

### 1.5 Schemas and solver contracts

| Object | Actual shape and consequential rules |
|---|---|
| Salary CSV | `Position, Name + ID, Name, ID, Roster Position, Salary, Game Info, TeamAbbrev, AvgPointsPerGame`, optionally `Status, Starting, Excluded`. IDs must remain strings; biological position and roster role are different fields |
| Reserved entries | Four identity/fee columns, then repeated roster labels; Classic uses ten slots, Showdown six. Instructions and embedded player pool may follow. Ordinary `DictReader` loses repeated `P`, `OF`, or `UTIL` columns |
| Classic projections | `Player_ID, Name, Team, Opponent, Position, Salary, Game_ID, Floor, Ceiling, Excluded, Locked`; materialized frames also carry Base, F1…F5, Base_Projection, source/mode/quality and batting-order metadata |
| Showdown pool | One physical-player row with `Player_Key`, distinct `CPT_ID`, `UTIL_ID`, corresponding salaries, Team, Base and participation annotations |
| MLB feed | Root `date, fetched_at, games`; each game has `game_pk, game_date_utc`, status, away/home sides, lineup status/order, probable pitcher and optional provider/DK IDs |
| Run manifest | `schema_version, run_id, mode, status, parent_run_id, inputs, artifacts, certification, metadata, environment`, hashes and relative paths |
| Delivery manifest | `date, version, deliveries[]`; delivered path/hash, run ID, slate tag, contest IDs, status, certification and strategy state |
| Standings | Positional entry side (`Rank, EntryId, EntryName, TimeRemaining, Points, Lineup`) plus player/role side (`Player, Roster Position, %Drafted, FPTS`); side lengths need not match |
| Ownership | Classic hitter/pitcher markets; Showdown captain and total-roster markets now separated. Historical field ownership and predictive ownership must remain distinct |

CSV schema inspection found 1,615 Classic-entry-shaped files, 150 Showdown-entry-shaped files, 768 salary files with the common 11-column schema, 459 standings files, 394 files with one common projection schema, and 308 assignment tables. These are counts of schema families, not necessarily unique slates or independent observations.

**Classic solve:** binary player-slot assignments; each slot filled once, each player at most once; P×2, C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, OF×3; salary ≤50,000; at most five hitters per team; at least two represented games; optional locks, excludes, team stacks, opposing-pitcher restrictions, overlap and ownership controls. The maximand is a Floor/Ceiling-derived adjusted score, with additional policy bonuses/penalties. It is not expected contest payout. See [optimizer_v3.py:857–1233](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/optimizer_v3.py:857>).

**Entry allocation:** binary candidate-entry assignments, one candidate per mutable entry; compatibility with locked slots and exclusions; contest duplicate/reuse, total and pitcher/player/stack/SP-pair caps, fixed-row headroom, and pairwise overlap. Shape-fit values are normalized per entry. Candidate filtering occurs before this MILP, so its optimality certificate covers the retained bank, not the complete lineup space. See [contest_allocator.py:2450–3519](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/allocate/contest_allocator.py:2450>).

**Showdown solve:** two binary roles per physical player; exactly one captain and five UTIL, mutually exclusive roles, actual role-specific salaries under the cap, and both teams represented. Captain points multiply by 1.5. Portfolio construction is a sequential thesis ladder, not a joint global expected-payout optimizer. Role-aware identity must be preserved separately from person-level overlap. See [showdown.py:382–621](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/showdown.py:382>), [showdown_theses.py:1010–1598](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/showdown_theses.py:1010>). The roster distinction is consistent with DraftKings' published Showdown overview; specific slate rules still require a versioned rule snapshot. [DraftKings Showdown overview](https://help.draftkings.com/hc/en-us/articles/24808583978003-Game-Style-Showdowns-Overview-US).

SciPy is the production MILP interface; PuLP/CBC/OR-Tools are not the active replacement solvers. SciPy status 0 is optimal, 1 a limit, 2 infeasible, 3 unbounded, and 4 another failure. A status-1 incumbent can be usable after validation; statuses 1/3/4 alone never prove infeasibility. [SciPy 1.15.3 MILP documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.15.3/reference/generated/scipy.optimize.milp.html).

### 1.6 Current repairs that should not be reported as still broken

- **R294 Classic allocator:** incompatible candidates no longer consume prefilter slots; per-entry reservation exists; a slate-level impossibility prevents the covered recursive relaxations; statuses 3/4 are not treated as proven infeasibility. The residual joint-coverage problem is F12, not the repaired incompatible-candidate problem.
- **R291 exclusion handling:** the main optimizer and bank enumeration use affirmative-token exclusion semantics; salary-origin exclusions are preserved in the normal front door. The refresh seam still has the separate F25 defect.
- **R304 pitcher geometry:** referee pitcher detection now checks biological Position for Showdown, and pitcher declarations are surfaced. The old blanket claim that CPT/UTIL hides all pitchers is obsolete.
- **R305 feed resolution:** the posted-lineup referee path now ranks compatible exact/superset game sets and rejects some ambiguous choices. Date/game identity and the separate lock-feed path remain incomplete (F22).
- **R306 ownership:** separate Showdown captain/roster markets and zero-ownership tail grading are present. The old claim that every Showdown prediction uses the Classic 1,000% market is obsolete. Marginal feasibility is still defective (F27).
- Missing late-swap status defaults to an error, empty explicit authorization is rejected, exact locked slots exist, and `validate_only` no longer claims optimization. Those improvements should be retained.
- Network helpers reviewed already set timeouts and scrub supplied odds secrets. This report does not repeat a generic “all network calls have no timeout” allegation.

## Section 2: Comprehensive Code Review & Defect Log

The findings below distinguish **reproduced** production-function behavior, **fault injection**, and **structural** reasoning. “Blocker” means a release/target capability blocker, not necessarily a crash in every front-door run. “Bug” means an incorrect reachable result or contract. Performance and Technical Debt findings identify measurable architectural causes without inventing benchmark results.

Corrected code is provided as complete helpers, surgical replacements, or explicitly identified integration seams. It is written to be pasted into the named module or a shared module as specified. It has not been applied to the repository, and syntax checking cannot establish production readiness: the acceptance checks listed with each finding and the pinned-runtime release suite remain required. Model estimation, migration of persistent state, and platform authorization cannot honestly be completed by a short code snippet.

### F01 — A legality validator can pass without salary evidence or any entries [Blocker]

**Location:** `mlb_engine/entries/dk_entries_manager.py:881–887, 928–959`, `validate_dk_entries_file`; [execution_pipeline.py:1163–1198](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/pipeline/execution_pipeline.py:1163>), `validate_salary_export`. **Evidence: reproduced.** One filled entry containing ten invented IDs passed without a salary file and with a header-only salary file. A header-only entries file passed with `entry_count=0`.

**Root cause / failure:** empty mappings disable membership, salary, position, team and game checks; an empty loop passes vacuously. The salary gate also accepts a file with merely one usable row. Higher-level callers sometimes supply better evidence, but the public validator's `passed` result is unsafe to reuse as legality certification.

**Correction:** insert these guards after the current `errors` initialization, preserving the existing full-row checks. Parse the salary into a list before making its map, so duplicates can be rejected. A structure-only inspection should have a separate result field and never report `FILE_VALID=true`.

```python
from collections import Counter
from math import isfinite

def release_input_errors(entries, salary_rows):
    errors = []
    if not entries:
        errors.append("no reserved entries parsed")
    if not salary_rows:
        errors.append("a nonempty salary table is required for legality")
    for label, ids in (
        ("Entry ID", [str(e.entry_id) for e in entries]),
        ("salary Player_ID", [str(p.player_id) for p in salary_rows]),
    ):
        duplicates = sorted(k for k, n in Counter(ids).items() if n > 1)
        if duplicates:
            errors.append(f"duplicate {label}: {duplicates}")
    for player in salary_rows:
        try:
            value = float(player.salary)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            value = float("nan")
        if not isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or not value.is_integer():
            errors.append(f"invalid salary for {player.player_id}")
    return errors
```

Replace the one-usable-row salary gate with complete schema/identity/value validation using the same input contract. **Acceptance:** all three reproduced cases fail; a corrupt extra salary row also fails; a genuinely valid complete template passes; duplicates are detected before dictionary collapse.

### F02 — Projection schema validation permits NaN, duplicate identity and negative salary [Blocker]

**Location:** [mlb_engine/optimize/optimizer_v3.py:456–468](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/optimizer_v3.py:456>), `validate_projection_schema`; [mlb_engine/projections/projection_builder.py:68–79](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/projections/projection_builder.py:68>), `validate_projection_factors`. **Evidence: reproduced.** Two same-ID rows with salary −1 and NaN Floor/Ceiling passed schema validation. Positive infinity also escapes the factor validator's NaN/negative tests.

**Root cause / failure:** column presence and `Ceiling < Floor` are insufficient. NaN comparisons are false; duplicate rows can map differently into solver indices and exported records. Invalid numerical inputs can crash the solve or invalidate the claimed problem.

**Correction:** add this shared validator at input, after enrichment, and before model construction; combine its errors with the current missing-field result. Validate additional enabled objective/control columns by the same finite rule.

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def numeric_projection_errors(frame):
    errors = []
    if frame.empty:
        errors.append("empty projection table")
    required = {"Player_ID", "Salary", "Floor", "Ceiling"}
    if required - set(frame.columns):
        return errors + [f"missing fields: {sorted(required - set(frame.columns))}"]
    ids = frame["Player_ID"].astype("string").str.strip()
    if ids.isna().any() or ids.eq("").any() or ids.duplicated().any():
        errors.append("Player_ID must be nonempty and unique")
    values = {}
    for column in ("Salary", "Floor", "Ceiling", "Base", "F1", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"):
        if column not in frame:
            continue
        vector = pd.to_numeric(frame[column], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
        values[column] = vector
        if not np.isfinite(vector).all():
            errors.append(f"{column} must be finite")
    salary = values["Salary"]
    if np.any(salary <= 0) or np.any(salary != np.floor(salary)):
        errors.append("Salary must contain positive integers")
    if np.any(values["Ceiling"] < values["Floor"]):
        errors.append("Ceiling is below Floor")
    return errors
```

**Acceptance:** empty, missing, duplicate, ±infinity, NaN and noninteger salary cases fail before SciPy. Do not impose nonnegative fantasy outcomes generically on future sports; validate the actual scoring contract.

### F03 — Supplied gate values bypass the guarded assumption mechanism [Blocker]

**Location:** [mlb_engine/pipeline/execution_pipeline.py:1068–1118](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/pipeline/execution_pipeline.py:1068>), especially line 1098, `resolve_gate_assertions`; `dk_entries_manager.py:146–154, 1113–1132`. **Evidence: reproduced.** A derived salary gate of `False` plus `supplied={salary_gate_passed: True}` returned `True`, with empty assumed/overridden/refused records.

**Root cause / failure:** a dictionary merge is a second authorization path around `OVERRIDABLE_GATES`. Elsewhere ordinary truthiness accepts objects such as nonzero numbers or nonempty containers. This does not mean callers can override the allocation result later in `execute_portfolio`; those fields are currently overwritten from the actual allocation. The exposed pre-export evidence seam remains defective.

**Correction:** replace line 1098 with this merge and extend `refused_records` with its refusals after the existing list is built. Keep permitted review-grade assumptions separately recorded; they cannot manufacture observed evidence.

```python
def merge_supplied_gates(defaults, supplied, derived):
    gates = dict(defaults)
    refused = []
```

### F04 — “Applied somewhere” is used as evidence of complete readiness [Blocker]

**Location:** [execution_pipeline.py:1121–1160](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/pipeline/execution_pipeline.py:1121>), `_applied`, and `1201–1381`, `_derive_workflow_gates`; [live_data_adapters.py:1035–1053](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/intake/live_data_adapters.py:1035>) records feed timestamps but does not itself enforce their freshness. **Evidence: structural.**

A transformation succeeding is different from every required fact being available.

**Correction:** use a field-scoped evidence decision. Required keys come from the slate/rule/model dependency graph, not from whatever rows arrived. Fixed-roof games can have an explicit `not_applicable` fact; they should not require a meaningless outdoor forecast.

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def evidence_errors(required_keys, facts, now, max_age_seconds):
    if now.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError("now must be timezone-aware")
    errors = []
    for key in sorted(required_keys):
        fact = facts.get(key)
        if not fact or fact.get("state") not in {"observed", "not_applicable"}:
            errors.append(f"{key}: evidence missing or conflicted")
            continue
        if not fact.get("source_sha256") or not fact.get("event_id"):
            errors.append(f"{key}: evidence identity missing")
            continue
        try:
            stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(fact["observed_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            if stamp.tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError("naive timestamp")
            age = (now.astimezone(timezone.utc) - stamp.astimezone(timezone.utc)).total_seconds()
            if age < 0 or age > max_age_seconds[key]:
                errors.append(f"{key}: stale or future evidence")
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            errors.append(f"{key}: invalid timestamp")
    return errors
```

**Acceptance:** one covered game cannot clear a three-game slate; fetched-at renewal cannot rejuvenate old provider observations; weather is checked per relevant game; required identity conflicts stay blocked. Review-grade computation can continue with a visible evidence state.

### F05 — Inputs are frozen after computation has already consumed them [Blocker]

**Location:** `execution_pipeline.py:4479–4511, 4843–4909`, `run_slate`; `309–358`, `execute_portfolio`; [build_state_manager.py:140–171](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/pipeline/build_state_manager.py:140>), `snapshot_run_inputs`. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** pool assembly, enrichment and bank construction precede the durable run snapshot. Later copies can differ from the bytes actually read. Reference/feed dependencies are not all forwarded as immutable inputs. A final hash proves the copied file, not the complete causal input set.

**Correction:** snapshot every dependency at intake and pass only those paths downstream. This helper names blobs by content and rejects a file changed during capture; add a source-role manifest and publish only after all captures succeed.

```python
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path

def freeze_input(source, blob_root):
    source = Path(source)
    before = source.stat()
    raw = source.read_bytes()
    after = source.stat()
    if (before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns) != (after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns):
        raise RuntimeError(f"input changed during capture: {source.name}")
    digest = sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    target = Path(blob_root) / digest
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if target.exists():
        if sha256(target.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
            raise RuntimeError("content-addressed blob is corrupt")
    else:
        atomic_write_bytes(target, raw)
    return {"path": str(target), "sha256": digest, "bytes": len(raw)}
```

Use F33's `atomic_write_bytes` in the same shared module: readers then see complete blobs. Serialize capture in the run actor, and require input producers to publish files atomically; comparing stat metadata alone cannot prove a read was coherent against an adversarial in-place writer. **Acceptance:** mutate an original after capture; all transforms still consume the captured bytes. Replays include salary, entries, feeds, reference versions, crosswalk, model, rules, policy, seed and code/runtime identity.

```python
    errors = []
```

### F07 — Manifest paths are not confined to the run [Security]

```python
from pathlib import Path

def confined_run_file(run_dir, relative_path):
    root = Path(run_dir).resolve(strict=True)
    rel = Path(relative_path)
    if rel.is_absolute() or rel.drive or ".." in rel.parts:
        raise ValueError("artifact path must be relative and confined")
    target = (root / rel).resolve(strict=True)
    if not target.is_relative_to(root) or not target.is_file():
        raise ValueError("artifact is not a regular file within its run")
    return target
```

**Acceptance:** traversal, absolute Windows paths, UNC paths, and escaping symlinks fail; ordinary nested artifacts pass. Hash verification remains mandatory after confinement.

### F08 — Atomic file replacement is mistaken for transactional publication [Bug]

**Root cause / failure:** compare-parent/read-modify-write and pointer/manifest writes occur in separate steps. Two processes can both pass the parent comparison and overwrite each other's delivery/current state. The “latest” pointer is not keyed by a complete slate/account/format identity. Directory claims guard initial acquisition but explicitly do not make release/retake atomic.

**Correction:** replace mutable shared pointers with a transactional store and compare-and-swap inside the same transaction. `scope` must include account namespace, provider draftgroup, sport, format and slate date; do not key only by date or display tag.

```python
import sqlite3

def publish_current(db_path, scope, expected_parent, new_run):
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0, isolation_level=None) as conn:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS current_run "
                     "(scope TEXT PRIMARY KEY, run_id TEXT NOT NULL)")
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT run_id FROM current_run WHERE scope=?", (scope,)).fetchone()
            current = row[0] if row else None
            if current != expected_parent:
                raise RuntimeError("parent changed; rebuild against current state")
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO current_run(scope,run_id) VALUES (?,?) "
                         "ON CONFLICT(scope) DO UPDATE SET run_id=excluded.run_id",
                         (scope, new_run))
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except BaseException:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
```

Publish only fully fsynced immutable bundles. Move delivery history into the same store, with JSON as a derived view, rather than retaining two authorities. Use a reliable local filesystem for SQLite; use a database service for multi-host coordination. **Acceptance:** racing writers produce exactly one winning parent transition; different slates coexist; crashes before commit leave the prior current state intact.

```python
import hashlib
import json

def problem_digest(player_records, rules, controls, objective, versions):
    rows = sorted((dict(row) for row in player_records),
                  key=lambda row: str(row["Player_ID"]))
    document = {
        "schema": "solve-problem-v1",
        "players": rows,
        "rules": rules,
        "controls": controls,
        "objective": objective,
        "versions": versions,
    }
    raw = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                     ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()

def admissible_candidates(candidates, validate_current):
    accepted, rejected = [], []
    for candidate in candidates:
        errors = validate_current(candidate)
        (rejected if errors else accepted).append(
            {"candidate": candidate, "errors": errors} if errors else candidate)
    return accepted, rejected
```

Canonical records must include all consumed fields with normalized primitive types. **Acceptance:** mutate each model/constraint dependency independently; key changes. Permuting rows does not. NaN fails. A candidate built under relaxed leverage cannot enter a stricter allocation merely because its player IDs still exist.

```python
import json
import sqlite3

def store_candidate(db_path, problem_key, roster, objective, job_key):
    roster_key = json.dumps(list(roster), separators=(",", ":"))
    payload = json.dumps({"roster": list(roster), "objective": objective,
                          "job": job_key}, allow_nan=False, sort_keys=True)
    with sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS candidates "
                     "(problem TEXT, roster TEXT, payload TEXT NOT NULL, "
                     "PRIMARY KEY(problem,roster))")
        conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO candidates VALUES (?,?,?)",
                     (problem_key, roster_key, payload))
```

Use a separate `(problem, job)` table for proven answers; query the requested problem key only. Retention deletes entire obsolete epochs independently of active writes. **Acceptance:** deletion never resurrects on reload; concurrent additions survive; a timeout is not inserted as an answered job.

```python
class SolverExecutionFailure(RuntimeError):
    pass

def _rung(latch, **call_kw):
    status = {}
    result = build_showdown_lineup(status_out=status, **call_kw)
    if result is None:
        if status.get("timed_out") is True:
            latch.update(timed_out=True,
                         message=str(status.get("message") or ""),
                         incumbent_rejected=status.get("incumbent_rejected") is True)
        elif status.get("proven_infeasible") is not True:
            raise SolverExecutionFailure(
                f"Showdown solve ended without a proof: {status.get('status')}")
    elif status.get("optimality") == "time_limited":
        latch["time_limited"] = True
    return result
```

### F17 — Showdown exposure accounting omits prefilled entries [Bug]

**Location:** `build_slate.py:3223–3230, 3294–3325`, `run_showdown`; [showdown_theses.py:1070–1138](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/showdown_theses.py:1070>), `solve_ladder`. **Evidence: structural.**

Individually valid new lineups can make the combined delivered portfolio violate the configured exposure policy. This is a portfolio-contract defect, not inherently platform illegality.

**Correction:** initialize all counts from fixed rows, use the combined denominator, and pass residual budgets into the joint allocator proposed in Section 4. This helper computes exact residual upper bounds without silently opening an already-exceeded cap.

```python
from collections import Counter
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_FLOOR

def exposure_headroom(fixed_rosters, total_entries, fraction):
    cap = Decimal(str(fraction))
    if not cap.is_finite() or not Decimal(0) <= cap <= Decimal(1):
        raise ValueError("exposure fraction must be in [0,1]")
    limit = int((cap * total_entries).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
    used = Counter(player for roster in fixed_rosters for player in set(roster))
    exceeded = {player: count for player, count in used.items() if count > limit}
    if exceeded:
        raise ValueError(f"fixed rows already exceed exposure cap: {exceeded}")
    return limit, {player: limit - count for player, count in used.items()}
```

Compute person and captain budgets separately, then per contest as required; absent keys have the full limit. **Acceptance:** mixed prefilled/blank templates satisfy the cap over all delivered entries; immutable violations are reported as unsatisfiable current policy, never silently repaired by changing locked rows. If policy intentionally uses ceil/minimum-one rounding, name it and report its realized percentage instead of pretending it is a strict fraction cap.

### F18 — The deadline does not bound the whole computation [Performance]

**Location:** `showdown_theses.py:1014, 1186–1454`; [contest_allocator.py:3152–3254](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/allocate/contest_allocator.py:3152>); `tools/autobuild.py:473–489, 541–565`; [bank_cache.py:557–564](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/bank_cache.py:557>); allocator overlap generation near `2998`. **Evidence: structural; no production latency benchmark claimed.**

**Root cause / failure:** each rung/recursion receives a new time limit. The supervisor checks time before launching another expensive child; serialization, process startup, projection rebuilding and validation sit outside many solver budgets. Repeated per-column sorting and dense candidate-pair construction add predictable overhead. The governor reacts to an already-computed refusal; it does not preempt that computation.

**Correction:** propagate one monotonic deadline across all stages, reserving time for validation/publication. Compile shared sparse matrices and sorted arrays once per snapshot; create variables only for compatible candidate-entry edges; generate overlap conflicts via player incidence or incremental cuts rather than all pairs when sparse.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from time import monotonic

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Deadline:
    end: float
    reserve: float = 0.0

    @classmethod
    def after(cls, seconds, reserve=0.0):
        if seconds <= reserve or reserve < 0:
            raise ValueError("budget must exceed nonnegative reserve")
        return cls(monotonic() + seconds, reserve)

    def remaining(self):
        return max(0.0, self.end - monotonic() - self.reserve)

    def slice(self, requested):
        budget = min(float(requested), self.remaining())
        if budget <= 0:
            raise TimeoutError("end-to-end compute deadline exhausted")
        return budget
```

Pass `deadline.slice(requested)` to every solver/subprocess; recursion inherits the same object. ### F27 — Predictive ownership can exceed 100% and contradict the roster market [Bug]

**Location:** [ownership_prior.py:676–727](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/field/ownership_prior.py:676>), `_showdown_prediction`, and Classic normalization near `491`; consumer acceptance at `824–896`, `attach_predicted_ownership`. **Evidence: reproduced.** Six players competing for six roster spots received ownership `[8.01,16.70,34.84,72.67,151.59,316.19]%`, totaling 600%. Each player must instead appear in every six-player roster in that constructed universe.

**Root cause / failure:** multiplying unconstrained softmax probabilities by roster-slot count enforces only the total, not each marginal's upper bound. Separate captain/roster predictions can also violate `captain <= roster`. Nonfinite/out-of-range external values are not uniformly rejected.

**Correction:** as an immediate numerical repair, project marginals onto the capped simplex. This guarantees market arithmetic, not calibration or a realizable distribution over every salary-constrained lineup. The target field model samples legal lineups and computes coherent marginals from them.

```python
import numpy as np

def capped_marginals(scores, slot_count):
    values = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
    if values.ndim != 1 or not np.isfinite(values).all():
        raise ValueError("finite ownership scores required")
    if not 0 <= slot_count <= len(values):
        raise ValueError("slot budget exceeds player universe")
    if slot_count == 0:
        return np.zeros_like(values)
    if slot_count == len(values):
        return np.ones_like(values)
    low, high = float(values.min() - 1.0), float(values.max())
    for _ in range(100):
        middle = (low + high) / 2.0
        if np.clip(values - middle, 0.0, 1.0).sum() > slot_count:
            low = middle
        else:
            high = middle
    return np.clip(values - (low + high) / 2.0, 0.0, 1.0)
```

Keep unrounded values internally; round only presentation and report any displayed rounding residual. Before using ownership controls reject missing/NaN/inf/out-of-range values, rather than treating missing values as attractive low ownership. **Acceptance:** six/six gives all ones; totals and bounds hold on thin and full pools; captain/roster coherence is enforced by the eventual joint model; held-out calibration is measured separately.

**Root cause / failure:** floor/ceiling multipliers are not learned quantiles; normalized fit scores erase monetary scale across contests. Salary, ownership and stack proxies cannot determine rank-dependent payouts, ties, duplicate splitting or portfolio returns. Current documentation often labels these proxies honestly, which is good; the capability still cannot satisfy the mandate's maximum-EV target.

**Correction:** introduce a settlement/evaluation interface before replacing the objective. The following exact tie-allocation primitive is ready for a settlement module; inputs must include all opponent and own scores and a complete frozen payout schedule. It does not estimate the outcome distribution.

```python
from fractions import Fraction

def settle_scores(scores, payout_cents_by_rank):
    if any(type(score) is not int for score in scores):
        raise ValueError("scores must use exact integer scoring units")
    if any(type(rank) is not int or rank < 1 or type(cents) is not int or cents < 0
           for rank, cents in payout_cents_by_rank.items()):
        raise ValueError("payout schedule must use positive ranks and nonnegative integer cents")
    ranked = sorted(enumerate(scores), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
    returns = [Fraction(0) for _ in scores]
    start = 0
    while start < len(ranked):
        end = start + 1
        while end < len(ranked) and ranked[end][1] == ranked[start][1]:
            end += 1
        total = sum(int(payout_cents_by_rank.get(rank, 0))
                    for rank in range(start + 1, end + 1))
        share = Fraction(total, end - start)
        for index in range(start, end):
            returns[ranked[index][0]] = share
        start = end
    return returns
```

Use exact scoring units; handle platform-specific cent rounding and noncash awards through an explicit rule adapter, not implicit float rounding. Section 4 specifies simulation, calibration, portfolio objectives and model admission. **Acceptance:** ties spanning paid/unpaid ranks conserve the applicable prize pool; identical roster scores tie naturally; own entries compete with one another; objective inputs are dollars with uncertainty and provenance. No production EV claim until prospective validation passes.

```python
from datetime import timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

def aware_utc(value):
    if value.tzinfo is None or value.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError("timestamp must include timezone")
    return value.astimezone(timezone.utc)

def eastern_clock(value):
    local = aware_utc(value).astimezone(ZoneInfo("America/New_York"))
    return f"{local.hour % 12 or 12}:{local.minute:02d} {'AM' if local.hour < 12 else 'PM'}"
```

```python
import json
import urllib.request

def fetch_bounded_json(request, timeout_seconds, max_bytes=16 * 1024 * 1024):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout_seconds) as response:
        raw = response.read(max_bytes + 1)
    if len(raw) > max_bytes:
        raise ValueError("provider response exceeds configured size limit")
    return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))

def validate_hourly_arrays(hourly, required_fields):
    times = hourly.get("time")
    if not isinstance(times, list) or not times:
        raise ValueError("weather timestamps missing")
    for field in required_fields:
        values = hourly.get(field)
        if not isinstance(values, list) or len(values) != len(times):
            raise ValueError(f"weather array is missing or misaligned: {field}")
    return len(times)
```

### F32 — ZIP ingestion can misattribute an existing CSV and consumes unbounded memory [Security]

**Location:** [tools/extract_inbox_zips.py:28–56](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/extract_inbox_zips.py:28>), `extract_zip`/`extract_inbox`. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** different ZIP members flatten to the same basename. An existing destination is returned as though it came from the current ZIP without comparing content. `src.read()` also decompresses an unlimited member into memory. This is a local downloaded-archive resource/provenance risk; basename extraction already avoids the simplest directory traversal and should not be falsely described as unrestricted `extractall`.

**Correction:** reject collisions and oversized members before writing. Preserve source archive/member hashes and never silently overwrite a differing existing CSV. This helper uses the atomic writer in F33.

```python
import hashlib
import re
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

def extract_csv_members(zip_path, destination, max_member=256 * 1024 * 1024,
                        max_total=1024 * 1024 * 1024):
    destination = Path(destination)
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    seen, output, total = set(), [], 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as archive:
        for member in archive.infolist():
            if member.is_dir() or not member.filename.lower().endswith(".csv"):
                continue
            name = PurePosixPath(member.filename.replace("\\", "/")).name
            if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._ -]*\.csv", name, re.I):
                raise ValueError("unexpected CSV member name")
            folded = name.casefold()
            if folded in seen:
                raise ValueError(f"duplicate archive destination: {name}")
            seen.add(folded)
            total += member.file_size
            if member.file_size > max_member or total > max_total:
                raise ValueError("archive exceeds configured extraction budget")
            with archive.open(member) as source:
                raw = source.read(max_member + 1)
            if len(raw) > max_member or len(raw) != member.file_size:
                raise ValueError("member size mismatch")
            target = destination / name
            digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
            if target.exists():
                if hashlib.sha256(target.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
                    raise ValueError(f"existing CSV conflicts with archive: {name}")
            else:
                atomic_write_bytes(target, raw)
            output.append({"path": str(target), "member": member.filename,
                           "sha256": digest})
    return output
```

Run extraction under the archive actor's exclusive destination ownership to prevent concurrent check/write races; forbid filesystem links in managed intake directories. **Acceptance:** conflicting basenames, differing existing files, corrupt CRC and oversized members fail with no misattributed success record; identical replays are idempotent. Preserve the original ZIP.

### F33 — Reference refresh overwrites live files before publishing a coherent generation [Bug]

**Location:** [tools/refresh_reference_data.py:579–624](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/refresh_reference_data.py:579>), `refresh`, especially 600 and 620; `_stamp:229–237`. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** validated text is written directly over live references. Concurrent readers can observe partial bytes or a mixture of generations; failure between the data write and manifest update leaves inconsistent state. Header/row-count validation does not make the write transactional.

**Correction:** write a complete reference generation into immutable content-addressed storage, validate its manifest, then publish its pointer transactionally (F08). This complete atomic writer is the immediate minimum for each file, not a substitute for generation-level publication.

```python
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

def atomic_write_bytes(path, raw):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, prefix=f".{path.name}.",
                                         suffix=".tmp", delete=False) as handle:
            temporary = Path(handle.name)
            handle.write(raw)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, path)
        temporary = None
    finally:
        if temporary is not None:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```

**Acceptance:** readers see complete old or complete new bytes; interruption leaves no promoted partial generation; manifest hashes identify exactly the reference data used. Filesystem durability beyond atomic replacement must be tested on the supported production storage.

### F34 — A declared “confirmed” feed is not validated as a complete lineup [Bug]

**Location:** [live_data_adapters.py:973–999](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/intake/live_data_adapters.py:973>), `build_status_map_from_lineups_feed`; direct feed consumers and declared pitcher parsing in [preflight_upload.py:1737–1744](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/preflight_upload.py:1737>). **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** the status-map function trusts the side's `lineup_status="confirmed"`, marks the team confirmed, and converts order values without requiring nine unique players/slots. Some upstream adapters validate more strongly, but direct callers and imported feeds bypass that protection. A partial or duplicate list can therefore establish wrong participation truth or throw during conversion.

**Correction:** validate facts at the shared boundary, not only at one producer. Use this for every side labeled confirmed before adding it to `confirmed_teams`; validate explicit pitcher-role values against the configured role enum before they can satisfy a role gate.

```python
def confirmed_order_errors(side):
    if str(side.get("lineup_status", "")).lower() != "confirmed":
        return []
    rows = side.get("lineup") or []
    ids, slots = [], []
    try:
        for row in rows:
            identity = row.get("dk_id") or row.get("id")
            if identity is None or not str(identity).strip():
                raise ValueError("player ID missing")
            if isinstance(row.get("order"), bool):
                raise ValueError("boolean order")
            ids.append(str(identity))
            slot = int(row["order"])
            if str(row["order"]).strip() != str(slot):
                raise ValueError("noninteger order")
            slots.append(slot)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return ["confirmed lineup contains an invalid ID/order"]
    if len(ids) != 9 or len(set(ids)) != 9 or sorted(slots) != list(range(1, 10)):
        return ["confirmed lineup must contain nine unique players in slots 1..9"]
    return []
```

**Acceptance:** confirmed empty/partial/duplicate/slot-10 feeds fail; valid full orders pass; projected partial lists remain projected. Explicit IDs still require F22's team/event check.

### F35 — Cached audit results do not cover the complete executable identity [Bug]

**Location:** [tools/audit.py:1588–1610](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/audit.py:1588>), `tree_fingerprint`, and compile check near 1172; dependency checks in [tools/env_probe.py:135–141](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/env_probe.py:135>); [requirements.lock:1–30](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/requirements.lock:1>). **Evidence: structural plus current runtime inspection.**

**Root cause / failure:** the audit fingerprint covers engine/tools/tests Python, omitting the 5,076-line skill build entry point and important configuration/reference dependencies. A cached unit result can survive a behavior-changing edit outside the fingerprint. The initial environment probe does compare installed versions with the lock; its post-install `_reprobe_subprocess` checks only import success, a weaker assertion. Explicit compile operations may create bytecode even when the audit is launched with `-B`.

**Correction:** fingerprint every executable/configuration/test-fixture input to the check, and bind results to runtime/package versions. Use `compile(source, path, "exec")` for a write-free syntax check.

```python
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

def audit_fingerprint(root, relative_paths, runtime_record):
    root = Path(root)
    records = []
    for relative in sorted(set(relative_paths)):
        raw = (root / relative).read_bytes()
        if relative.endswith(".py"):
            compile(raw.decode("utf-8-sig"), relative, "exec")
        records.append((relative, hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()))
    payload = {"files": records, "runtime": runtime_record,
               "fingerprint_schema": "audit-v2"}
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True,
                                    separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
```

The path list must be derived from a reviewed manifest that includes `skills/generate-lineups/scripts`, requirements, rules, test fixtures and dependency metadata; tests must not choose their own narrower fingerprint. **Acceptance:** changing only `build_slate.py`, a relevant rule or a dependency version invalidates cached results; syntax inspection leaves the source tree unchanged.

### F36 — The supported runtime is not available on this Windows host [Blocker]

**Location:** [requirements.txt:1–20](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/requirements.txt:1>), [requirements.lock:1–30](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/requirements.lock:1>), `tools/env_probe.py`; current host observations in Section 1. **Evidence: directly verified.**

**Root cause / failure:** the lock contains Linux/Python-3.10 wheel hashes, while the available Windows environments do not have a compatible verified SciPy runtime. The bundled pandas 3.0.1 also exceeds the project's `<3` requirement. This blocks local solver certification and makes “copy/paste anywhere” operations depend on environment repair at the worst time.

**Correction:** designate and prewarm a pinned execution image; add an independently resolved/hashed Windows lock only if Windows is a supported solver target. Do not claim that an alternate runtime's partial tests certify Linux. A strict admission check can be:

```python
import importlib.metadata
import platform
import sys

def runtime_admission():
    expected = {"numpy": "2.2.6", "pandas": "2.3.3", "scipy": "1.15.3"}
    actual, errors = {}, []
    for package, version in expected.items():
        try:
            actual[package] = importlib.metadata.version(package)
        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            actual[package] = None
        if actual[package] != version:
            errors.append(f"{package}: expected {version}, got {actual[package]}")
    if sys.version_info[:2] != (3, 10) or platform.system() != "Linux":
        errors.append("runtime is outside the current Python 3.10/Linux lock")
    if platform.machine().lower() not in {"x86_64", "amd64"}:
        errors.append("runtime architecture is outside the current lock")
    return {"passed": not errors, "packages": actual, "errors": errors}
```

Admission also needs a real MILP smoke solve and wheel/image hashes; metadata alone cannot validate binary compatibility. **Acceptance:** pinned image passes all required suites and a real end-to-end fixture; other runtimes are explicitly structural/supplemental until separately admitted. No environment was installed or changed during this audit.

### F37 — Supervisor success is inferred from exit zero and loosely parsed prose [Bug]

**Location:** [tools/autobuild.py:275–287](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/tools/autobuild.py:275>), `parse_brief`, and `596–600`; review-grade delivery paths in [build_slate.py:3203–3950](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/skills/generate-lineups/scripts/build_slate.py:3203>). **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** the parser depends on JSON whitespace/key order and searches mixed stdout for a status object. Exit zero is then logged as “certified,” even though build paths intentionally deliver review-grade artifacts. A delivered file, successful process and certified release are different states.

**Correction:** emit one versioned result JSON file separately from human stdout, then validate it and its artifact hash. Classification must read explicit facts and never promote a label based on return code alone.

```python
def classify_build_result(return_code, result):
    if result.get("schema") != "build-result-v1":
        return "protocol_error"
    if return_code != 0:
        return str(result.get("failure_class") or "execution_error")
    if result.get("delivered_sha256") is None:
        return "protocol_error"
    facts = ("FILE_VALID", "EVIDENCE_VALID", "SELECTION_VALID", "ALLOCATION_VALID")
    if all(result.get(key) is True for key in facts) and result.get("RELEASE_DECISION") == "READY":
        return "certified_release"
    return "delivered_review_grade"
```

The supervisor must independently verify the delivered hash and scope before treating even `READY` as current. Strategy/model certification remains a separate dimension. **Acceptance:** review-grade exit zero stays review-grade; missing/invalid JSON is a protocol failure; reordered JSON and noisy stdout cannot change interpretation; resume does not use an old successful attempt as the current result.

### F38 — Bank iteration completion is reported as answered search [Bug]

**Location:** `bank_cache.py:858–946, 983`, `extend_bank`; `tools/autobuild.py` bank growth decisions near 636. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** `exhausted` can remain true when the loop visits every job but all jobs raise, time out, or return no proof. Those jobs correctly stay out of `attempted`, yet `job_list_exhausted` suggests no useful retry remains. This undermines the repaired distinction between answered and unanswered jobs.

**Correction:** keep enumeration, attempted work and completed answers as distinct fields. Compute completion from exact job IDs and admissible terminal states.

```python
def bank_progress(job_ids, answers):
    jobs = set(job_ids)
    answered_states = {"optimal", "proven_infeasible"}
    answered = {job for job in jobs if answers.get(job) in answered_states}
    pending = sorted(jobs - answered)
    return {"jobs_total": len(jobs), "jobs_answered": len(answered),
            "jobs_pending": pending,
            "search_complete": bool(jobs) and not pending,
            "empty_job_grid": not jobs}
```

A validated limited incumbent may be a usable candidate while its search job remains unfinished. **Acceptance:** all-error/all-timeout sweeps retain pending work; fully proven jobs complete; an empty job grid is diagnosed separately from a solved slate.

### F39 — Independent pivot counts are not proof of a feasible late-swap escape [Bug]

**Location:** [late_swap_manager.py:138–160](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/swap/late_swap_manager.py:138>), `_eligible_for_pivot`, `pivot_requirements_for_tbd_players`. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** each uncertain player independently counts candidates under a local salary buffer and position intersection. A candidate can already be rostered; several uncertain slots can depend on the same alternatives; replacing multiple players can exceed the actual residual salary or violate team/game rules. Two nominal pivots per player do not prove one feasible whole-lineup repair.

**Correction:** keep the current counts as diagnostics only. Certify reserve feasibility by solving the actual residual roster with exact fixed slots, remaining salary, exclusions and the same rules, then independently validate the returned lineup. The orchestration seam must require all those checks:

```python
def certify_pivot_reserve(request, solve_residual, validate_residual):
    result = solve_residual(request)
    if result.get("solution") is None:
        return {"passed": False,
                "state": "infeasible" if result.get("proven_infeasible") is True else "unknown"}
    errors = validate_residual(request, result["solution"])
    return {"passed": not errors, "state": "feasible" if not errors else "invalid",
            "errors": errors, "witness": result["solution"],
            "optimality": result.get("optimality", "unproven")}
```

Both callbacks must be the typed residual solver and independent rule validator, not tests of the same heuristic counts. Include shared scratch scenarios rather than assuming one-at-a-time news. **Acceptance:** two slots with the same sole reserve, an already-rostered pivot, and collectively unaffordable swaps fail; a genuine legal residual witness passes.

### F40 — Showdown captain reservations can outlive the slots they reserve [Bug]

**Location:** [showdown_theses.py:1116–1124](<C:/Users/benja/Documents/Claude/mlb-dfs/mlb_engine/optimize/showdown_theses.py:1116>), reservation initialization; UTIL blocking near 1280; release at `1474–1475`. **Evidence: structural.**

**Root cause / failure:** holds are bounded by captain demand/cap but not the total player cap. Holds are spent when the actual selected captain appears, rather than when the requested captain's scheduled opportunity has been processed. A failed/substituted requested captain can leave a phantom hold blocking later UTIL choices; an incidental earlier captain can consume a later reservation.

**Correction:** bound reservations by both budgets, track the remaining requested slots, and release the current request's hold exactly once at the end of its slot, whether it succeeds, substitutes or fails. Replace initialization and the actual-captain decrement with these respective fragments:

```python
reserve_ceiling = min(
    cpt_cap if cpt_cap is not None else len(theses),
    player_cap if player_cap is not None else len(theses),
)
reserved_remaining = {key: min(count, reserve_ceiling)
                      for key, count in captain_demand.items()}

# At the end of processing each thesis slot, including an empty result:
if want_cpt is not None and reserved_remaining.get(want_cpt, 0) > 0:
    reserved_remaining[want_cpt] -= 1
```

The stronger fix is a joint role-aware portfolio allocator: it eliminates reservation order dependence entirely. **Acceptance:** substituted, failed, incidental and repeated captain cases consume the right requested hold; no remaining hold exceeds the remaining player/captain headroom; combined fixed-row exposures from F17 are honored.
