## Section 3: Greenfield System Audit & Anti-Pattern Deconstruction

### 3.1 What is essential, what should change, and what can be retired

| Current component/pattern | First-principles decision | Replacement or retirement condition |
|---|---|---|
| Exact platform CSV parsing, immutable inputs, final-byte hashes | Keep and strengthen | These establish identity and prevent accidental entry corruption; centralize one contract |
| SciPy/HiGHS MILP | Keep as a baseline engine | There is no evidence here that changing solver brands fixes the observed trust, identity or scheduling failures |
| Classic/Showdown eligibility and salary constraints | Keep as tested adapters | Move rules into versioned data; have an independent referee derive legality from the same authoritative rule snapshot through different code |
| Multiple feed/clock/parent resolvers | Consolidate | One event identity, evidence registry and lock service per snapshot; all entry points consume it |
| Base/F1…F5 and APPG-derived bounds | Retain as explicitly labeled baseline features | Replace claimed distributions only when a learned outcome model wins prospective admission tests |
| Thesis multipliers and normalized shape scores | Retain for candidate diversity experiments | Stop using their magnitudes as interchangeable portfolio utility; evaluate candidates under one outcome/field/settlement model |
| Sequential Showdown exposure/hold ladders | Replace | Shared role-aware candidate bank and joint entry allocator, with typed strategy relaxation only after appropriate proof |
| JSON union cache and mutable latest pointers | Replace | Immutable problem namespaces plus transactional jobs, manifests and publication |
| Repeated full CLI/subprocess build loops | Remove from the hot path | Warm service owns arrays, solver templates, evidence versions and monotonic budgets; CLI becomes an API client |
| Pasted evidence workflows | Keep as optional ingestion adapters | They can seed structured facts but never bypass schema, identity, freshness or source retention |
| LLM-authored ad-hoc roster changes | Remove from numerical execution | Deterministic minimum-change repair with frozen slots and independent final-file checks |
| Mandatory rereading of long histories | Retire from routine context | Small active contract plus indexed, task-specific retrieval of decisions and incidents |
| Ignored scratch mutation/patch scripts | Archive from discoverable execution paths | Preserve history as requested; exclude from runtime imports/tool routing and package allowlist. Do not delete existing work during this audit |
| Duplicate delivery/status authorities | Replace | One durable run/result schema and transactional publication event; rendered JSON/Markdown are views |
| Manual entry/financial boundary | Preserve on the current platform | Replace only with a documented authorized provider capability and explicit standing account policy |

No broad repository deletion is justified merely to make a directory smaller. The immediate throughput gain comes from stopping historical/scratch code and prose from participating in runtime decisions, then removing redundant paths after parity tests. File count itself is not the main latency cost.

### 3.2 Context and instruction engineering

`CLAUDE.md` is 811 lines / 54,829 characters; `skills/generate-lineups/SKILL.md` is 1,301 lines / 74,629 characters. Together they contain about 129,458 characters, roughly 32,365 tokens using the crude four-characters-per-token heuristic—not a measured tokenizer count. `changelog.md` alone is 15,330 lines / 1,098,308 characters. `NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md` is another 203 lines / 11,497 characters. Long decision/backlog ledgers add further retrieval cost.

The problem is not simply length. Behavioral rules, exceptions, incident narratives, historical test counts, temporary environment workarounds, monetary policy, solver semantics and user preferences coexist in several places. An agent can obey a stale explanatory paragraph while violating current code. Repeating a rule in five files does not make the executable boundary enforce it five times; it creates five opportunities for drift.

The current instructions also contain valuable distinctions: legal pool versus search effort; file validity versus strategy quality; review-grade delivery versus certified release; and deterministic local arithmetic versus language-model reasoning. Preserve those distinctions in typed program state. Their current prose volume reflects repeated incidents where a missing executable contract had to be explained to the next session.

Recommended progressive disclosure:

1. **Root contract, approximately 1,000–1,500 tokens:** authorized workflow entry point, current run/result schema, protected evidence/entry boundaries, exact environment command, task routing and links. No incident chronology or mutable counts.
2. **Machine-readable runtime manifest:** rule/model/provider versions, supported formats, dependency image, required checks, result fields and failure enums. Generate a short human view from it.
3. **Task playbooks:** intake, build, late swap, archive, incident response, implementation review. Load only the selected playbook and the referenced contract.
4. **Decision registry:** one short record per durable decision, with status, scope, effective date, superseded-by link, source evidence and tests enforcing it. Historical narratives remain searchable by ID.
5. **Session context:** exact snapshot/run ID, current failures, pending jobs, deadline and changed facts. It replaces free-form “where we left off” reconstruction.

Measure improvement through tokens read per successful run, unnecessary build restarts, contradictory status reports, time to locate an applicable decision, and incident recurrence—not by a subjective claim that a shorter prompt is smarter. Prompt-size targets above are implementation targets, not current measurements.

### 3.3 LLM versus deterministic boundaries

| Work | Owner | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Parse IDs, numbers, CSV fields, salary totals, payout tables | Deterministic code | Exactness, reproducibility and cheap validation |
| Structured provider polling and schema changes | Typed adapter + schema monitor | A changed contract must not silently become a new fact |
| Unstructured injury/news interpretation | Optional bounded LLM extractor | It can propose structured claims with quoted evidence, source URL, event/player candidates and uncertainty |
| Identity confirmation | Deterministic crosswalk service | A language model's plausible name match is insufficient to move numerical evidence |
| Projections, ownership, simulations, optimization, settlement | Local numerical services | Replays, measured calibration, common random numbers and numerical error control |
| Strategy experiment design and exception diagnosis | Human or LLM research layer | Hypotheses are useful when separated from production coefficients and release authority |
| Run state, retry, deadline, risk limits, export and submission state | Deterministic orchestrator | These are durable operational contracts, not conversational judgments |
| Explanations and final handoff | LLM over a typed result | Clear communication without recomputing or changing the result |

An extraction model should receive only the relevant source excerpt and canonical candidate identities, return a fixed schema, and have no ability to mark evidence verified, mutate entries or invoke a monetary action. Contradictory news produces a conflict event. Optional model assistance must never sit on the hot path for ordinary structured MLB updates.

### 3.4 Why the present system stalls

The dominant failure pattern is boundary duplication: the system repeatedly re-derives “what slate is this,” “which feed applies,” “what is locked,” “what did the solver prove” and “what does success mean.” Monolithic command tools then compensate with retries, warning interpretation and document-driven escalation. A successful return in one layer does not imply another layer's contract.

Additional latency comes from repeated process/import startup, full DataFrame copies per thesis, repeated sorting/hashing, Python loops to construct sparse constraints, repeated solver setup, per-entry normalization and O(K²) overlap work. Historical filesystem scans for input discovery or archive names should not occur inside a lock-window solve. These are structural costs; this audit did not measure a representative production latency profile under SciPy.

Zero-touch execution should mean that every event has a deterministic next action and durable outcome. It does not mean fabricating a missing starter, ignoring a platform lock, or claiming an unknown solver state is infeasible. An unresolved job can remain pending, finish as abstained, or publish a clearly labeled review artifact while other slates continue. The orchestrator must not block a worker waiting for a conversational answer.

The deadline governor's distinction between delivering a partial review artifact and certifying it is useful. Preserve it. Its trigger must operate on correct typed failures and a real end-to-end budget; a delivery deadline cannot change evidence truth or platform editability.

## Section 4: Target Greenfield Architecture & Implementation Specs

### 4.1 Scope and non-negotiable output truths

Implement MLB Classic and MLB Showdown first because those are the repository's actual supported formats. Provide versioned sport/rule interfaces for NFL, NBA, soccer, golf, other single-game multiplier variants and Tiers. Do not claim those adapters are implemented or use MLB roster counts for them. Each adapter requires its own official scoring/roster/lock snapshot and contract fixtures before admission.

Every result must expose independent fields:

```json
{
  "schema": "dfs-result-v1",
  "snapshot_id": "content digest",
  "run_id": "unique immutable run identifier",
  "FILE_VALID": false,
  "EVIDENCE_STATE": "UNKNOWN",
  "MODEL_STATUS": "UNCALIBRATED",
  "SEARCH_STATUS": "NOT_RUN",
  "SEARCH_SCOPE": "NONE",
  "PORTFOLIO_POLICY_STATE": "NOT_CHECKED",
  "RELEASE_DECISION": "DO_NOT_UPLOAD",
  "SUBMISSION_STATE": "NOT_ATTEMPTED",
  "reason_codes": [],
  "artifact_sha256": null
}
```

Enumerate allowed values in a schema; examples above are conservative defaults, not inferred facts. `FILE_VALID` means exact exported bytes satisfy the platform/template/entry contract. `EVIDENCE_STATE` records completeness, freshness and conflicts. `MODEL_STATUS` distinguishes a projection proxy, research estimate and admitted calibrated model. `SEARCH_STATUS` describes proof/limits/failure; `SEARCH_SCOPE` states single lineup, restricted bank or full modeled problem. An optimal candidate-bank allocation is never silently upgraded to globally optimal EV.

Separate artifacts may be delivered for review even when release is blocked. Release policy must be a pure function of verified facts and standing user policy, not a field supplied by a caller. A user-approved proxy workflow may be a distinct operational policy; it must retain `MODEL_STATUS=PROXY` and cannot call itself EV-certified.

### 4.2 Module architecture and ownership

```text
dfs/
  contracts/       rules.py, identity.py, evidence.py, results.py, policy.py
  providers/       mlb.py, weather.py, odds.py, projections.py, platform_intake.py
  storage/         blobs.py, snapshots.py, event_log.py, jobs.py, publication.py
  identity/        crosswalk.py, event_resolver.py
  evidence/        reconcile.py, freshness.py, participation.py, locks.py
  features/        common.py, mlb.py, point_in_time.py
  models/          outcome.py, workload.py, field.py, calibration.py, registry.py
  simulate/        games.py, field_sampler.py, score.py, scenarios.py
  optimize/        legal_model.py, candidate_bank.py, portfolio.py, deadline.py
  settlement/      payout.py, ties.py, tickets.py, portfolio_returns.py
  release/         byte_csv.py, referee.py, transition.py, decision.py
  submission/      capability.py, outbox.py, receipts.py
  orchestrate/     slate_actor.py, scheduler.py, recovery.py
  reporting/       review.py, explanations.py, metrics.py
```

| Module boundary | Input → output | Hard rule |
|---|---|---|
| Provider adapter | Request/event identity → raw bytes + retrieval metadata | No mutation of canonical state; bounded I/O, source time, payload hash and request identity |
| Identity | Provider facts + salary/rule snapshot → exact crosswalk | Ambiguity is a typed unresolved record; never choose by fuzzy score alone |
| Evidence reducer | Versioned facts → reconciled immutable slate snapshot | Source precedence is field-specific; newer retrieval is not necessarily newer evidence |
| Feature builder | Snapshot + feature/model version → finite arrays | Point-in-time availability and complete dependency hashes |
| Outcome model | Features + participation/workload state → joint outcome generator | Distribution parameters and admitted support documented; no fabricated quantile interpretation |
| Field model | Contest snapshot + projected popularity → legal opponent portfolios | Role marginals, salaries, eligibility and within-user dependence respected |
| Candidate service | Snapshot/rules/model/policy → legal candidate bank + search status | Full legal universe retained; pruning only reduces search effort and is recorded |
| Portfolio service | Bank + entries/fixed rows + scenarios → assignments and risk estimates | Combined portfolio economics, exact identities, shared deadlines |
| Referee | Final bytes + immutable sources + parent → independent checks | No caller booleans; validate all actual bytes and changed slots |
| Publisher | Validated bundle + expected parent → current run | Transactional compare-and-swap, scoped by full slate identity |
| Submission adapter | Authorized capability + ready export → receipt/reconciliation state | Idempotent intent, bounded retry, unknown outcome distinguished from rejected |

Use a local relational store for jobs, event offsets, leases, current pointers and immutable-record indexes. Large arrays and raw inputs belong in hash-addressed files/object storage. JSON/Markdown are interchange/review views. A per-slate actor serializes state transitions; independent slates and provider fetches can run concurrently under explicit I/O and CPU budgets.

### 4.3 Canonical data contracts

**Slate identity:** provider, provider draftgroup ID, sport, format/rule version, slate date, exact event IDs, scheduled times and legs. Human labels such as “7g main” are display metadata, not keys. Account-specific entries are a separate scoped object.

**Player identity:** physical person ID, provider IDs, platform role-specific ID, event ID, team ID, biological positions, eligible roster slots, exact integer salary and eligibility/status facts. Showdown role rows share one person but retain separate export IDs and salary values. An identity crosswalk binds the salary hash and source evidence.

**Evidence record:** field name, entity/event key, value, provider observation time, retrieved time, source document hash, parser version, valid interval, state, precedence and conflicting alternatives. Fields such as roof status, probable starter and workload are separate facts. A forecast is not roof evidence; projected participation is not confirmation.

**Contest contract:** contest ID, field size/filled state, authorized entry IDs, entry fees in integer cents, exact payout schedule or typed noncash awards, maximum entries, scoring period, edit/late-swap rules and rule source hash. Unknown payout tiers block expected-payout certification. Contest-name archetypes may initialize a research prior but cannot replace the actual economics.

**Snapshot:** immutable roots for salaries, entry template, events, evidence, references, crosswalk, rules, model, policy, runtime/code version and seeds. Every derived artifact records its immediate parents and snapshot digest. No transform rereads a mutable global reference path after snapshot creation.

**Run:** deterministic input/config identity plus unique execution ID, started/heartbeat/finished times, resource budget, solver/problem status, candidate/search scope, final export hash, independent check results and expected parent revision. Creation of a file is not a terminal success condition.

### 4.4 Complete roster and portfolio formulation

Let `E` be authorized entries, `P` physical players, `S` roster slots and `G` events. Let `a[p,s] ∈ {0,1}` denote eligibility, `c[p,s]` the actual role-specific salary, `m[s]` the scoring multiplier, and `B` the salary cap if the format has one. Let `x[e,p,s] ∈ {0,1}` and `u[e,p] = Σ_s x[e,p,s]`.

For each entry:

```text
Σ_p x[e,p,s] = 1                              for every required slot s
x[e,p,s] ≤ a[p,s]                             eligibility
Σ_s x[e,p,s] ≤ 1                              one physical person per lineup
Σ_p,s c[p,s] x[e,p,s] ≤ B                      when a salary cap exists
x[e,p,s] = 0                                 if ineligible/excluded under the frozen request
x[e,p,s] = parent[e,p,s]                       for immutable locked slot assignments
```

Eligibility is a platform/rule fact. Participation/model uncertainty is represented separately. Do not remove legal players merely to meet a compute deadline. An operational policy may forbid certain statuses, but the exclusion and reason must be explicit and versioned.

For MLB Classic set `S = {P1,P2,C,1B,2B,3B,SS,OF1,OF2,OF3}`, `B=50,000`, and all `m=1`. Biological pitcher eligibility and multi-position hitter eligibility determine `a`. For each team `t`, let `H_t` be its hitters:

```text
Σ_p∈H_t u[e,p] ≤ 5
y[e,g] ≤ Σ_p in g u[e,p] ≤ |S| y[e,g]         y[e,g] binary
Σ_g y[e,g] ≥ 2
```

The game upper/lower bounds force `y` to represent actual usage. Do not replace the game rule with a team-count approximation. A both-teams/specific-event rule uses the format's actual definition.

For MLB Showdown set `S={CPT,UTIL1,…,UTIL5}`, one physical person at most once, `m[CPT]=1.5`, remaining multipliers 1, and at least one player from each of the two teams. Use actual CPT and UTIL salary/export IDs from the source, not recomputed rounded prices. Person exposure uses `u`; captain exposure uses `x[e,p,CPT]`. MVP/STAR or other multiplier formats use their own slot multipliers and salary rules—neither is inferred from the other.

For Tiers, eligibility maps each player to the appropriate tier slot and exactly one player is selected per required tier. Apply a salary constraint only if the versioned platform contract actually defines one. NFL/NBA/soccer/golf adapters define their own slot counts, flex eligibility, scoring, team limits, participation and lock rules; no MLB stack rule is inherited automatically.

**Optional stacking policy:** let `h[e,t]=Σ_p∈H_t u[e,p]`, and `z[e,t]` choose a designated primary team. When a primary stack is required:

```text
Σ_t z[e,t] = 1
h[e,t] ≥ L z[e,t]
h[e,t] ≤ U + |S|(1-z[e,t])
h[e,t] ≥ h[e,v] - |S|(1-z[e,t])               for all other teams v, if primary means largest
```

Keep the ordinary team maximum independently. Specify a deterministic tie rule for the diagnostic primary label. A bring-back lower bound can be activated by `z`. Opposing-pitcher limits are strategy, not general MLB legality:

```text
Σ_h opposing pitcher p u[e,h] ≤ q + |S|(1-u[e,p])
```

**Exposure policy:** let `N` include both mutable and fixed entries in the scope. A strict upper fraction `α` becomes `floor(αN)`; a lower fraction `β` becomes `ceil(βN)`. Record this integerization. Do not force a minimum count of one while claiming a literal small percentage cap.

```text
ceil(β_p N) ≤ fixed_count[p] + Σ_e mutable u[e,p] ≤ floor(α_p N)
fixed_cpt[p] + Σ_e mutable x[e,p,CPT] ≤ floor(α_cpt,p N)
```

Apply corresponding team-stack/SP-pair/contest limits with their own explicit scope. For a pitcher pair `(i,j)`, binary `w[e,i,j]` obeys `w≤u_i`, `w≤u_j`, `w≥u_i+u_j−1`; sum `w` plus fixed counts against its cap. If immutable rows already violate a cap, return a policy conflict, not a negative residual bound disguised as a solver problem. Policy relaxation requires a recorded policy transition; locks and platform legality never relax.

**Overlap:** for entries `e,f`, person overlap is `Σ_p u[e,p]u[f,p]`. Binary `v[e,f,p]` can linearize it with the same three AND constraints, then `Σ_p v≤M`. Role-aware exact duplication is separate. In a candidate bank, precompute person bitsets and captain-aware signatures, then add only relevant conflict cuts; do not eagerly materialize every candidate pair when it is avoidable.

**Candidate-to-entry assignment:** let `K` be a versioned legal candidate bank and `b[e,k] ∈ {0,1}` indicate all current-entry compatibility checks. Let `y[e,k]` be binary:

```text
Σ_k y[e,k] = 1                               each mutable entry assigned once
y[e,k] ≤ b[e,k]                              exact lock/identity/control compatibility
Σ_e y[e,k] ≤ reuse_cap[k]                     scope explicit; subtract fixed reuse where applicable
Σ_e in contest, k with signature σ y[e,k] ≤ 1 - fixed_uses[contest,σ]
Σ_e,k contains p y[e,k] + fixed_count[p] ≤ player_cap[p]
```

The same incidence construction covers captain/team/SP-pair quotas. Conflict inequalities `y[e,k]+y[f,l]≤1` cover prohibited overlap. Avoid empty candidate sets/entries passing vacuously. A restricted-bank infeasibility first expands the search domain; it cannot justify relaxing a full-bank strategy constraint.

### 4.5 Outcomes, ownership, settlement and the actual EV objective

Generate scenarios `ω=1…W` from a **joint** game/outcome model conditioned on the immutable point-in-time evidence. The player score vector is `F[p,ω]`. The score of entry `e` is:

```text
Q[e,ω] = Σ_p,s m[s] F[p,ω] x[e,p,s]
```

For MLB, model team plate appearances, batting-order opportunities, pitcher workload/removal, handedness, opponent quality, park/weather effects and shared game conditions. Correlation follows shared events: one plate appearance simultaneously affects hitter and opposing-pitcher outcomes; teammates share inning/run opportunities. Independent normal noise around APPG cannot represent that mechanism. Calibrate appearance/workload distributions separately from conditional performance. Extra innings, bullpen roles, substitutions, postponement/suspension scoring and slate-specific rules require explicit treatment.

For other sports, use sport-specific event/workload modules: snap/route/touch and game-script structure for NFL; minutes/usage/pace for NBA; minutes, set pieces and scoring events for soccer; round/hole outcomes and cut/withdrawal states for golf. These are model requirements, not claims that a single covariance matrix already solves them.

Sample opponent **legal portfolios**, conditional on contest type/field size and population characteristics. Marginal ownership alone is insufficient: it does not identify stacks, captains, duplicated lineups, salaries left, or dependence among a user's multiple entries. Separate captain and total-roster markets and require `0≤captain_p≤roster_p≤1`, sums 1 and 6 respectively in a six-person Showdown format. Deriving marginals from legal lineup samples enforces more coherence than independent softmax columns. Record model uncertainty and alternative field scenarios.

For contest `c`, combine every simulated opponent score and every selected own-entry score. For entry `e`, let `A[e,ω]` be the number strictly above it and `T[e,ω]` the number tied with it, including itself. If `V[c,r]` is the cash payout at rank `r`, its scenario gross return is:

```text
G[e,ω] = (Σ_r=A[e,ω]+1 … A[e,ω]+T[e,ω] V[c,r]) / T[e,ω]
R[ω]   = Σ_e G[e,ω] - Σ_e fee[e]
EV_hat = (1/W) Σ_ω R[ω]
```

Apply the actual platform tie/rounding rule and represent tickets/noncash awards as typed outcomes. Ticket face value is not automatically cash-realizable EV. Missing prize tiers or field size prevent a verified expected-payout claim. Already-reserved fees are constant in a swap's incremental optimization, but remain in reported total portfolio economics.

The target optimization is:

```text
maximize  E_model[R(portfolio)]
subject to platform legality, fixed entries/slots, entry authorization,
           standing exposure/concentration policy and optional risk constraints.
```

Risk policy can constrain probability of zero gross return or CVaR of loss `L=-R`. For confidence level `a`, a sample CVaR representation is:

```text
CVaR_a(L) = min_eta [eta + (1 / ((1-a)W)) Σ_ω z[ω]]
z[ω] ≥ L[ω] - eta; z[ω] ≥ 0
CVaR_a(L) ≤ approved_limit
```

An alternative objective `EV_hat - λ CVaR` is a risk-adjusted utility and must be labeled as such. The coefficients/limits come from standing user policy, not arbitrary optimizer defaults. Maximizing mean payout alone does not mathematically guarantee a smaller chance of a zero-return slate.

**Critical computational distinction:** if candidate utility is precomputed against opponents alone, ignoring own entries' rank/tie interaction, the resulting additive MILP is an approximation. It is not the exact nonlinear portfolio settlement objective above. Use it as a proposal/master problem, evaluate complete portfolios with exact scenario settlement, then perform bounded candidate exchanges or decomposition. Return “best evaluated feasible portfolio” unless the actual modeled objective has a valid global bound/proof. For small test problems, enumerate every legal portfolio and compare the master/search result to the exact optimum.

Candidate diversity and integer programming are well-established research directions, but a published method is not validation of this repository's coefficients or profitability. The target adapts those ideas under explicit local calibration and payout tests. [Hunter, Vielma and Zaman, Picking Winners in Daily Fantasy Sports Using Integer Programming](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.01455).

### 4.6 Calibration, experimental separation and model admission

1. Freeze point-in-time features, provider observations and forecasts before lock; never overwrite them with postgame knowledge. Every feature must have `available_at ≤ prediction_cutoff`.
2. Split by slate/event/date, not randomly by player row or contest. Many contests on the same game share outcomes and are not independent validation samples.
3. Use separate DESIGN data for models/hypotheses, SELECT data/scenarios for choosing candidates and policies, and REFEREE data/scenarios for final evaluation. Do not keep tuning against the final referee seed set.
4. Use common random numbers when comparing competing portfolios within a stage. Report paired differences and Monte Carlo standard error; independent stage seeds reduce selection overfit. For fixed independently sampled scenario returns, `SE(mean)=sample_sd/sqrt(W)`; clustered/serial data require the corresponding cluster-aware uncertainty calculation.
5. Validate outcome means, dispersion, quantile coverage, tails, participation/workload and covariance; validate ownership/role-market calibration, lineup duplication and construction frequencies; validate settlement separately with exact hand examples.
6. Run a prospective shadow period with frozen forecasts and actual slate results. Compare against explicit baselines using matched slates/fees and uncertainty intervals. Historical retrospective fit is insufficient to establish prospective EV.
7. Admit a model version only under prespecified coverage, calibration, drift and economic-evaluation criteria, with uncertainty and sample-size limitations recorded. No universal profitable threshold is invented here.

The model registry binds training data/time range, code, parameters, feature schema, admitted sports/formats, calibration report and expiry/drift policy. Missing model admission automatically selects a labeled proxy/research mode or abstention according to standing policy; it cannot relabel a projection sum as dollars.

### 4.7 Sub-second service specification

The feasible target is **warm response under a declared workload envelope**. Network retrieval, model training, large simulation generation and exhaustive combinatorial search occur outside the synchronous request. A cold arbitrary slate cannot honestly be promised an exact global EV optimum within one second.

Proposed, unmeasured service objectives for an admitted workload (for example MLB ≤400 physical players, ≤150 authorized entries, and a prevalidated bounded candidate bank):

| Stage | Target budget | Design |
|---|---:|---|
| Read immutable current snapshot / event delta | 25 ms | In-memory version pointers; no directory scans |
| Update affected features and legality/lock mask | 75 ms | Column arrays; event/player dependency index |
| Candidate refresh + bounded portfolio search | 500 ms | Warm bank, cached matrices, prior feasible incumbents and strict monotonic deadline |
| Independent checks on exact planned export | 100 ms | Deterministic integer/bitset checks plus independent parsing |
| Atomic artifact/publication work | 100 ms | Small writes, pre-created run scope, transactional current pointer |
| Reserve | 200 ms | Scheduling variance and safe fallback |

These sum to a one-second budget, not a measured SLA. Acceptance must measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end on named hardware, concurrency and representative large/small/slate-change fixtures. Report timeout rate, feasible-incumbent availability, search scope, objective quality on enumeratable cases, peak memory, CPU-seconds and provider cost per slate. No benchmark excludes final validation or pretends a bank lookup generated a new exact optimum.

Use legal cached incumbents when unchanged facts still support them. When a scratch invalidates one, repair only affected entries against fixed slots, then evaluate the complete portfolio. If no valid feasible incumbent exists before the deadline, publish a typed failure/review artifact; retain prior platform state only if it remains valid. Do not silently submit a stale lineup to hit a latency number.

### 4.8 Zero-touch operational loop

1. **Prewarm before slate windows:** admit runtime image, solver, schema/model/rule versions, storage health and clock synchronization. Recover expired jobs and reconcile pending submission outcomes. No dependency installation at T−5.
2. **Discover and register slates:** use an authorized provider feed/API or user-provided immutable platform files. Resolve exact draftgroup/events/format. Unknown formats enter `unsupported_contract`, with other slates continuing.
3. **Register authorized entry scope and policy:** snapshot existing entry IDs, contest economics, spending/entry constraints and deadline policy. An ordinary build may fill existing authorized entries; new purchases require separately established standing authorization/capability.
4. **Collect evidence asynchronously:** fetch independent structured sources concurrently with provider-specific rate limits, bounded payloads, retries and monotonic request budgets. Poll faster near relevant event locks within provider limits; deduplicate unchanged payload hashes. Persist raw evidence before interpretation.
5. **Resolve identities and conflicts:** join exact IDs and event legs; apply field-specific source precedence/freshness. Schedule a bounded alternate-source attempt for missing/conflicted facts. Do not block a worker waiting for chat; unresolved facts remain pending or terminally unavailable.
6. **Create a new immutable snapshot:** include all required source versions, active participation/lock state, references, rules, crosswalk, model and policy. Compute its digest before numerical work.
7. **Update arrays/scenarios/bank:** rebuild only dependencies invalidated by the event delta. Preserve the legal universe; distinguish policy exclusion from search truncation. Revalidate candidates under the new problem digest.
8. **Optimize and evaluate:** fill mutable entries jointly against fixed rows, preserve exact locked slots, honor residual budgets, and evaluate complete portfolios under the chosen model. Report solver proof/limit state and estimated-value uncertainty independently.
9. **Referee the actual export:** emit a provisional immutable CSV; parse its exact bytes independently; validate schema, row identity, salaries/roles/positions/games, complete authorized assignments, lock transitions, controls, snapshot/source hashes and model/release policy. Recheck the lock/evidence version immediately before publication.
10. **Publish transactionally:** compare the expected current revision with the active scoped revision. If it changed, discard the stale promotion attempt and rebase the computation; never overwrite newer news. Record the final digest and derived release decision.
11. **Submit only through an admitted capability:** outbox intent includes exact entry set, parent revision, artifact digest, standing authorization and idempotency key. The current DraftKings adapter remains export-only absent express platform authorization; an authorized alternative/partner API can implement the fully automated branch.
12. **Verify receipt and watch for changes:** persist platform acknowledgment and readback/reconciliation. An accepted request without confirmed entry state is `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN`, not success. Continue relevant evidence/lock monitoring until no authorized mutable entries remain.
13. **Late scratch/swap:** consume the newest accepted parent, preserve all locked cells, apply status and workload changes, regenerate only invalidated candidates, reoptimize residual entries and repeat steps 8–12 under one remaining-time budget.
14. **Settle and learn:** ingest immutable actuals/standings, reconcile missing contests and payout types, settle exact historical returns, grade the frozen prediction/model, and add observations to the research queue. Production coefficients do not self-update from one slate's result without model admission.

The loop has deterministic terminals: ready/exported, submitted/verified, review-grade, abstained, unsupported, failed, or submission-unknown. Unavailable essential evidence produces a durable reason and future event subscription, not an endless retry or an instruction for an LLM to guess. An alert may request exception resolution, but no worker or unrelated slate waits for it.

DraftKings documents that entry/edit closure and late-swap availability depend on contest/game rules. Therefore game start data and platform editability must remain distinct facts, and the adapter must freeze the actual contest rule instead of assuming one universal lock behavior. [DraftKings entry/edit closure guidance](https://support.draftkings.com/dk/en-us/when-do-lineup-entries-and-edits-close?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0010806).

### 4.9 Exact-byte export and submission contract

The export writer should lex the original CSV bytes into row/field spans while respecting quoted commas, escaped quotes, embedded newlines, BOM and original line endings. Modify only the spans for authorized roster cells. Export values are the exact role-specific platform IDs; all other byte spans remain identical. Preserve fixed/locked cell bytes exactly, not merely their normalized player IDs. Reparse the generated bytes through a separate positional parser before final hashing.

Tests must include repeated headers, CRLF/LF, BOM/no-BOM, quoted names/commas, multiline quoted instructions, trailing empty columns, embedded pool tables, fully/partially populated templates, repeated player-role IDs, blank authorized rows and unauthorized additions. Reject ambiguous/malformed CSV; do not repair it silently. SHA-256 binds final bytes to the run and the receipt.

The submission capability interface must declare platform, operation, account scope, supported formats, authorization source/expiry, idempotency semantics, rate limits and readback capability. Its default state is disabled. The proposed intent key is a digest of account namespace, draftgroup, authorized entry IDs, expected platform revision and export hash.

Use a transactional outbox: commit intent before sending, then record attempt and receipt. A network timeout after sending is an unknown outcome. Retry only using the same provider idempotency key or after authoritative reconciliation; if neither is supported, stop that intent as unknown rather than risk duplicate entry purchases or overwriting a newer lineup. Do not claim distributed exactly-once side effects without provider support.

The current repository's manual-DraftKings boundary is supported by the live terms review, not merely an arbitrary architectural preference. Full autonomous submission is a **capability dependency**, not a hidden implementation step. The rest of the architecture remains useful and autonomous under an export-only capability.

### 4.10 Implementation order, acceptance gates and measurable exit criteria

| Stage | Concrete scope | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A — Truth and export boundary | F01–F09, F19–F24, F34, F37; typed result schema, strict source/identity validation, parent transitions, durable failure and publication | Reproduced false passes eliminated; both referees agree; exact-byte fixtures; concurrency/fault-injection checks; pinned runtime passes |
| B — Search correctness and orchestration | F10–F18, F25, F30–F33, F38–F40; full problem keys, transactional cache, typed solver outcomes, shared deadlines, joint Showdown/fixed-row accounting | No computational error changes strategy; full-bank recovery; no stale reuse; deadline reserve honored; small enumerations match legal optimum |
| C — Identity/evidence and warm service | Exact crosswalk/event service, immutable reference generations, provider jobs, array/matrix caching | Complete replay from snapshot; no live mutable dependency reads; schema drift and provider outages yield typed outcomes; measured warm latency distribution |
| D — Outcome/field/settlement research | F26–F29; joint models, legal opponent sampler, exact payout and own-entry interaction, independent experimental splits | Settlement oracle passes; coherent ownership; point-in-time training; calibrated prospective shadow results with uncertainty |
| E — Capability-based operation | Durable scheduler/outbox, scoped standing policies, authorized provider integration if available, receipt reconciliation | Crash/retry/idempotency scenarios pass; no unsupported platform automation; submission-unknown never reported accepted |
| F — Additional sports/formats | Versioned adapter and scoring/lock/eligibility tests per requested sport | Official rule snapshot, real platform file fixtures, scoring oracle, independent legality and appropriate model admission |

Preserve existing engine outputs as comparison baselines while replacing one boundary at a time. Archive superseded paths only after end-to-end parity tests and documented routing changes; do not mass-delete history. Test financial/entry/lock/identity/publication boundaries aggressively. Avoid hundreds of shallow tests that merely assert copied constants or mock away the defect under review.

The first production milestone is a truthful, replayable, deadline-bounded engine that reliably produces valid artifacts with correct status. The second is a prospectively evaluated expected-payout model. Combining them yields the intended autonomous decision system; calling the present proxy pipeline EV-certified would skip the evidence needed to know whether it works.

### 4.11 Deliverable verification

The report contains **40 findings: 12 Blockers, 25 Bugs, 2 Security findings and 1 Performance finding**, plus the instruction/architecture debt analysis in Section 3. The inventory includes all 12,812 enumerated files and all 3,871 first-party function/method definitions. All 40 Python blocks parse; 24 focused checks passed on extracted proposed helpers, including strict inputs, gate merges, path confinement, publication compare-and-swap, ownership bounds, tie settlement and lock transitions. Those helper checks are separate from the **465 passing existing repository tests** and do not establish full integration or real-solver certification.

Final filesystem verification on September 8, 2026 at 09:41 CDT found all **1,140 intake-hashed files unchanged**, with none missing. The expanded inventory's **10,981 hashed files** were also unchanged, with none missing. The sole new normal workspace file was this dated specification. All 249 generated local file links resolved, including their cited line starts. Prior specifications, tracked modifications, untracked work, ignored run outputs and reference data were preserved; no production fix, dependency installation, entry edit or upload was performed.

The remaining verification dependency is the admitted Python 3.10/Linux/SciPy runtime: run the complete required suite, real solver/adversarial fixtures, integration of any selected patches, and representative end-to-end timing there before calling an implementation ready. This document reports current evidence and a concrete implementation specification; it does not certify a live slate or promise profitability.
